Caching and batching impact on unit economics

transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. with me is Daniel, our solutions eng.
[00:08] Sofia Ramirez: Thanks, Maya. We have about 45 minutes. we're most interested in how your console surfaces cost and how we can map our routes to different models.
[00:18] Daniel Cho: Great, we'll jump into the console - first thing you'll see is the usage analytics home. top-left is time range, then per-route cards.
[00:30] [screen-share sound] Daniel Cho: So here's Verdant's example routes - search-autocomplete, summary, and personalization. each route has throughput, p50/p95 latency, token counts. you can click a route to get a breakdown by model and by API key.
[00:52] Priya Shah: That per-route split - is that automatic, or do we need to add metadata on our side?
[00:58] Daniel Cho: By default it's based on the route param you pass to our API. you can also tag requests server-side for finer slices. small caveat - if you proxy a lot of calls through a single route, tags help.
[01:12] Liam O'Connor: How granular are the cost numbers? Do we get per-request, per-token cost?
[01:19] Maya Patel: Yes - we show aggregates and sample request cost. the cost model combines model unit rates, token counts, and your committed discounts. you'll see per-route cost-per-1000-tokens, and a waterfall that attributes cost to model selection, batching efficiency, and cache hits.
[01:36] Daniel Cho: Here's an example - search-autocomplete is cheap per token but very high qps; personalization uses a larger context and a more expensive model. the console estimates monthly spend and shows recommended lever changes - e.g., suggest quantized variant or smaller base model for tail requests.
[01:53] Sofia Ramirez: Does the console simulate batching gains or is that from real historical runs?
[01:58] Daniel Cho: It's mostly historical; we model potential gains from changing your autoscale/batching knob. the optimizer module can run what-if analyses - if you enable continuous batching or increase max-batch-size, the estimated per-token cost drops by X but p95 could increase.
[02:15] Priya Shah: Can we export these dashboards to CSV? we'll want to push into our internal chargeback system.
[02:20] Maya Patel: Absolutely - CSV/JSON exports for any dashboard, plus an API if you want automated pulls.
[02:26] [slight crosstalk] Liam O'Connor: ok, security. we need VPC/private deployment and KMS integration. where do those show up?
[02:35] Daniel Cho: On the account page we have a "deployments" tab. for Private customers we surface node-level metrics; KMS keys and audit logs are accessible through the security tab. we also attach per-token logs to the audit trail (redacted by default).
[02:48] Sofia Ramirez: SOC2 and retention - will you be able to meet our 7-year log retention?
[02:53] Maya Patel: SOC2 is standard; retention is an add-on - we can accommodate long-term retention via our archive tier. I'll send the SOC2 cert and retention options.
[03:02] Daniel Cho: Back to cost - here's the per-route view. note the orange highlight: 12% of tokens are hot prefixes that can be cached. enabling prefix caching reduced cost by 18% in a comparable customer.
[03:18] Priya Shah: Are those cache savings modeled conservatively? we worry about regen quality with cached prefixes.
[03:24] Daniel Cho: Good point - the optimizer flags prompts where prefix caching may change semantics and gives a confidence score. you can opt-in per-route.
[03:33] [pause, keyboard sounds] Daniel Cho: Now I'll open the model catalog panel - you can compare performance profiles. for a route like personalization we recommend a gpt-3.8-ish equivalent quantized to 4-bit for Dedicated, or a hosted large variant if you prefer managed ops.
[03:52] Sofia Ramirez: What about fallbacks? if a dedicated pool is saturated, do you fallback to hosted without changing tokens drastically?
[03:59] Maya Patel: Yes - smart routing policies let you fallback across capacity tiers or model variants. you can set cost-first or latency-first policies per-route.
[04:08] Liam O'Connor: How accurate are the cost projections for a pilot vs production?
[04:13] Daniel Cho: For pilot, projections are based on a sample replay of your traffic and our runtime's simulated batching and KV cache. it's usually within 10-15% once you normalize for peak patterns.
[04:24] Sofia Ramirez: We have a lot of short-requests - seq lengths < 64 for autocomplete but long threads for summary. will your per-route recommendations handle mixed distributions?
[04:35] Daniel Cho: Yes - the console shows seq length distributions per route and suggests different model variant or quantization by percentile. you can pin a route to a variant for 10% of traffic as a canary.
[04:46] Maya Patel: Quick demo of the cost waterfall for a single day - model base cost 62%, batching inefficiency 18%, cache misses 20%. toggling continuous batching to aggressive cuts inefficiency to 8% but raises p95 by ~40ms.
[05:05] Priya Shah: That tradeoff seems reasonable. Do you provide automated A/B experiments for quality/regression?
[05:11] Daniel Cho: Yup - rollout controls, canary percentage, and quality monitors tied to prompt sets. if quality regressions exceed thresholds, auto-rollback can trigger.
[05:20] Sofia Ramirez: Who do we work with on the pilot? we'll need SE time to run replays and benchmarks.
[05:26] Maya Patel: Daniel will own the pilot technical setup with your infra team. we'll also pull in a solutions architect depending on scale.
[05:32] Daniel Cho: I'm going to open the "what-if" optimizer. you can set target p95 and cost budget; optimizer suggests model mix, batching knobs, and caching rules to meet budget. here I've set p95 < 300ms and budget $40k/mo, it recommends: 70% hosted small-variant, 20% dedicated quantized, 10% fallback large.
[05:56] Liam O'Connor: Sounds useful. For metrics we need export to our Prometheus - is there a push option?
[06:01] Daniel Cho: There's a tracing and metrics export; Prometheus scrape endpoints for metrics are available for Dedicated/Private. Hosted API gives you push webhooks for alerts.
[06:10] Sofia Ramirez: Any customers in retail doing similar routing?
[06:13] Maya Patel: Yes - a mid-market retail chain reduced unit cost by 28% after changing their model mix and enabling prefix caching; we can share an anonymized case study.
[06:22] Priya Shah: What about tokenization differences - we use multiple languages and often see tokenization variance.
[06:28] Daniel Cho: The console shows tokens per-language and normalizes cost. tokenizer mismatches are called out in the prompt diagnostics.
[06:35] Sofia Ramirez: Ok, let's talk timeline - we want a pilot in the next two weeks. can you replay a week's worth of traffic?
[06:44] Daniel Cho: Yes - we can replay via a secure transfer; for PII we can run in-situ in your VPC or anonymize before transfer.
[06:52] Maya Patel: I'll follow up with an email that outlines the pilot steps, datasharing options, and estimated Redwood hours.
[06:59] Liam O'Connor: Great. last question on pricing - do you provide committed discount tiers for Dedicated?
[07:05] Maya Patel: Yes - reserved capacity discounts are available; we'll include a pricing sheet in the follow-up.
[07:11] Priya Shah: One more thing - is there a way to tag routes by product team for chargeback?
[07:16] Daniel Cho: Yep, route tags map to owner metadata and appear in the per-route cost table; you can ingest those via API to your chargeback system.
[07:25] Sofia Ramirez: Sounds promising.
[07:28] Maya Patel: Recap - we'll send pricing, SOC2, and pilot runbook. Daniel will coordinate replay and bench. Priya to share traffic characteristics.
[07:36] Sofia Ramirez: Thanks, Maya & Daniel.
[07:38] Maya Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up.
[07:42] [call ends]
